title: Developer Experience: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site ops, and top support issues
author: Aisha Patel
summary: Canonical playbook for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: structure and conventions for SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and the canonical list of top support issues with fixes. This page is the single-source-of-truth for authors and support engineers producing or maintaining end-user SDK/docs artifacts.
body:
Overview

Purpose:
- Provide a single, searchable playbook for consistent SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operating procedures, and canonical support fixes.
- Reduce time-to-first-success for customers and lower support load by ensuring docs and examples are high quality and triageable.

Audience:
- Developer Experience writers and engineers
- SDK maintainers and API owners
- Developer support and solutions engineering

Ownership and SLA:
- Primary owner: DevEx (eng-developer-experience)
- Reviewers: Platform SDK leads and SRE for runtime-sensitive examples
- Update cadence: Quarterly review for each SDK guide and quickstart; critical fixes as-needed.

Document structure and conventions
- Use short, descriptive titles (dash-separated file names).
- All guides must include: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step quickstart, expected output, troubleshooting section, and links to related pages.
- Use code blocks for runnable examples; include both curl and at least one language SDK (Python or Node).
- Keep copy concise and action-oriented; prefer numbered steps for tasks.
- Example tag usage: labels: [devex, sdk, python, quickstart]

SDK Guides (required sections)
1) Overview: intent and recommended use cases.
2) Compatibility matrix: supported model families, API versions, and minimum SDK versions.
3) Installation: pip/npm examples and verification commands.
4) Quickstart: runnable example that returns a simple success response within 60s.
5) Configuration: runtime flags, environment variables, and recommended timeouts.
6) Error handling: common errors and suggested retry/backoff policies.
7) Testing & CI: unit test snippet and local emulator instructions.
8) Changelog & migration notes.

Sample SDK Quickstart (Python)
1) Prerequisites:
   - Python 3.10+
   - API key (REQUIRED) set in REDWOOD_API_KEY
2) Install:
   pip install redwood-sdk>=1.8.0
3) Minimal example:

```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
import os
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate(text="Translate to French: Hello world")
print(resp.text)
```

Expected output: translated text (string). If the SDK raises a 401, confirm the key and environment variable.

API Examples (curl + Node)
- curl example:

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Summarize: The quarterly report..."}'

- Node (fetch) example:

```js
import fetch from 'node-fetch';
const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Summarize: Cloud cost report' })
});
const data = await res.json();
console.log(data.output[0].content);
```

Docs-site Operating Procedures (publish + rollback)
- Branching: content is authored in markdown in the docs repo; each doc gets a single branch per feature (docs/FEATURE-123).
- Review process:
  1) Author opens PR (use docs-template).
  2) Assign DevEx reviewer and one SDK owner (automated CODEOWNERS).
  3) Run site-local build (`make site-build`) and smoke test examples in samples/
  4) Merge after approvals and a green build.
- Publishing:
  - Merges to main trigger CI to publish a draft to staging (docs.redwood.dev/staging).
  - QA: DevEx performs smoke tests on staging; test scripts must run in <10 minutes.
  - Final publish to prod after staging sign-off.
- Rollback procedure (urgent production issue):
  1) Revert merge commit in docs repo (git revert -m 1 <merge-sha>).
  2) Trigger CI to republish.
  3) Notify #devex and #support channels with rollback reason and follow-up task.

Quality gates and automated checks
- Linting: markdownlint and custom rules (no TODOs, no hard-coded keys).
- Link checks: nightly link-checker job; failures create tickets in the docs backlog.
- Example verification: CI runs smoke examples from the examples/ directory against the staging API; failures block merge.
- Accessibility: run axe-core checks on key pages (tutorials + quickstarts).

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (operational playbook)
- Purpose: give support engineers a short triage path with an authoritative fix for each frequent issue.

| Issue ID | Symptom | Likely root cause | Canonical fix | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DX-101 | SDK install fails with wheels error on M1 macs | Binary wheel not available for the platform | Recommend `pip install redwood-sdk --no-binary :all:` and add note in pip install section; track upstream wheel builds | SDK team |
| DX-203 | 401 Unauthorized from examples | Expired/missing API key or wrong environment variable | Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY, rotate key if compromised; add clear error text in SDK (401 -> helpful message) | Security/SDK |
| DX-317 | Streaming responses truncate for long outputs | Default client-side timeout shorter than server chunking | Increase client timeout to 120s or enable streaming-specific handler; update quickstart to use stream reader | SDK/SRE |
| DX-425 | Examples fail in corporate proxy environments | Proxy blocks outbound requests or TLS MITM | Document proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY), provide cURL with --proxy option, and recommend service account token with corporate-approved CA | DevEx/Security |
| DX-512 | Broken code snippet in published page | Upstream API change or copy-paste error | Reproduce locally, open PR with fix, run example smoke test, and add automated snippet test in CI | DevEx |

Canonical triage checklist (for support runbook)
1) Reproduce the failure with the same OS/SDK/API version.
2) Collect logs: SDK debug output, request ID, timestamp, region.
3) Check status dashboard and recent deploys.
4) Apply the canonical fix.
5) Create a docs PR if root cause is docs-related; add regression test.

Templates and PR checklist (copy into new quickstarts)
- Quickstart template (required sections): title, one-line summary, prerequisites, install, run steps, expected result, troubleshooting, related links.
- PR checklist (authors must run):
  - [ ] Local site build passes
  - [ ] Examples smoke tests pass against staging
  - [ ] Linting and link-check pass
  - [ ] Assign reviewers and update related_pages
  - [ ] Add labels and confidentiality

Maintenance and versioning guidance
- API breaking changes: create migration guide and keep old examples marked with `deprecated` header for 90 days.
- SDK version pinning: examples should pin to `redwood-sdk>=x.y.z` and include a note when relying on experimental features.

Appendix: Example troubleshooting snippet (collecting logs)
- Python SDK debug (env):
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...
  export RW_SDK_LOG_LEVEL=debug
  python -m redwood.examples.translate

- Provide these artifacts when filing internal ticket: logs, request-id, full payload, timestamps, and reproducible minimal example.

Contact and escalation
- Primary channel: #devex (triage during 9:00-18:00 PT)
- After-hours: pager duty (on-call DevEx) and #oncall-alerts.
- For security-sensitive incidents, follow security-and-compliance/incident-response-security playbook.
